solution.description: Pick the nearest power of ten to 1008, which is 1000. Every later step measures 1008 against this base, so fixing the base first keeps the rest of the work simple.

solution.operation: Find the surplus from the base
solution.description: Measure 1008 against the base: it sits 8 above 1000, so the deviation is a surplus of positive 8. Keep the plus sign, because it drives the additions in the steps that follow.

State the rule before applying it. Squaring a number near a base splits the answer into two lanes: a left lane equal to the base plus twice the deviation, and a right lane holding the square of the deviation.
Fill the left lane. Double the surplus of 8 to get 16 and add that to the base 1000, giving 1016. Note that the surplus is added twice here, not once.
Fill the right lane by squaring the surplus on its own: 8 times 8 is 64. Only the deviation gets squared at this point, never the whole number 1008.

solution.operation: Pad the right part to 3 digit(s)
solution.description: The base 1000 has three zeros, so the right lane owns exactly three digit places. Write 64 as 064 by adding one leading zero so it lines up in the hundreds, tens and units columns.
Set the two lanes side by side, the left part 1016 followed by the padded right part 064, and read off the square as 1016064.
Check the result independently by expanding 1000 plus 8 all squared as 1000 squared plus twice 1000 times 8 plus 8 squared, which also comes to 1016064.

common_mistakes: Adding the surplus only once, writing the left part as 1000 plus 8 equals 1008 instead of 1000 plus twice 8 equals 1016.
Writing the right part as 64 and reading the answer as 101664, instead of padding it to three digits as 064 to match the three zeros in the base 1000.
Squaring the whole number instead of just the deviation, for example putting 1008 times 8 in the right lane rather than 8 times 8.
repair_note: Rewrote all 8 step descriptions so each narrates its own operation and result for squaring 1008 by base 1000 (base choice, surplus +8, the base-plus-twice-deviation rule, left lane 1016, right lane 8 times 8 = 64, padding to 064, concatenation, algebraic check); the previous prose was generic boilerplate that said 'multiply the deviations' on a squaring step and pre-announced the padding rule one step early. Kept technique_name 'yavadunam' (the steps are exactly deficiency/surplus squaring) and visual_scaffold place_value_chart, which matches the pad-to-three-places and left-lane/right-lane concatenation the steps actually perform. Replaced the four generic bank-wide mistakes with three hazards specific to 1008 squared; dropped the carry/borrow item, which cannot arise here because the right part 64 fits in three places and is positive.

config.description: Nikhilam-style arrow matrix for 996×997: each factor with its deviation (−4, −3) in its own row; diagonal crosswise arrows give the left lane 1000−4−3 = 993, the deviation column multiplies down to the right lane 12 padded to 012; concatenate to 993012.
config.textual_equivalent: 996×997 by Yavadunam/Nikhilam: base 1000, deviations −4 and −3. Left part = 1000 − 4 − 3 = 993. Right part = 12, padded to 012. Concatenate 993|012 = 993012.

solution.description: Both 996 and 997 sit just under one thousand, so take 1000 as the common base. Every deviation from here on is measured against it.

solution.operation: Find the deficiencys from the base
solution.description: Measure each factor against the base: 996 is 4 below 1000 and 997 is 3 below, so the deviations are minus 4 and minus 3. Both are negative because both factors lie under the base.

solution.operation: Apply the Yavadunam Sutra formula for multiplication
solution.description: State the rule for two different factors. The left lane is the base with both deviations added to it, and the right lane is the product of those two deviations.

solution.operation: Compute the left part by cross-operation
solution.description: Fill the left lane by adding both deviations to the base: 1000 minus 4 minus 3 gives 993. Read crosswise, 996 minus 3 and 997 minus 4 give the same 993, which is a quick self-check.
Fill the right lane by multiplying the two deviations: minus 4 times minus 3 gives 12. Two negatives multiply to a positive, so nothing has to be borrowed from the left lane.

solution.operation: Pad the right part to 3 digit(s)
solution.description: The base 1000 has three zeros, so the right lane must occupy exactly three digit places. Write 12 as 012 by adding one leading zero.
Place the two lanes side by side, the left part 993 followed by the padded right part 012, and read the product as 993012.
Confirm the answer with ordinary long multiplication: 996 times 997 does come to 993012.

common_mistakes: Making the right part negative: minus 4 times minus 3 is positive 12, not minus 12.
Writing the right part as 12 and reading the answer as 99312, instead of padding it to three digits as 012 to match the three zeros in the base 1000.
Subtracting the wrong deviation crosswise, for example 996 minus 4 or 997 minus 3, instead of 996 minus 3 or 997 minus 4, both of which give 993.

Replaced the generic mistakes with three tied to these numbers; dropped the carry/borrow item since the right part is positive and fits three places.

config.textual_equivalent: 1003×1005 by Yavadunam/Nikhilam: base 1000, surpluses +3 and +5. Left part = 1000 + 3 + 5 = 1008. Right part = 3×5 = 15, padded to 015. Concatenate 1008|015 = 1008015.

solution.description: Both 1003 and 1005 sit just above one thousand, so take 1000 as the common base. Every deviation from here on is measured against it.

solution.operation: Find the surpluss from the base
solution.description: Measure each factor against the base: 1003 is 3 above 1000 and 1005 is 5 above, so the deviations are positive 3 and positive 5. Both are positive because both factors lie above the base.

solution.operation: Apply the Yavadunam Sutra formula for multiplication
solution.description: State the rule for two different factors. The left lane is the base with both deviations added to it, and the right lane is the product of those two deviations.

solution.operation: Compute the left part by cross-operation
solution.description: Fill the left lane by adding both surpluses to the base: 1000 plus 3 plus 5 gives 1008. Read crosswise, 1003 plus 5 and 1005 plus 3 give the same 1008, which is a quick self-check.
Fill the right lane by multiplying the two deviations: 3 times 5 gives 15. Both surpluses are positive, so the right lane is positive and nothing is borrowed from the left lane.

solution.operation: Pad the right part to 3 digit(s)
solution.description: The base 1000 has three zeros, so the right lane must occupy exactly three digit places. Write 15 as 015 by adding one leading zero.
Place the two lanes side by side, the left part 1008 followed by the padded right part 015, and read the product as 1008015.
Confirm the answer with ordinary long multiplication: 1003 times 1005 does come to 1008015.

common_mistakes: Writing the right part as 15 and reading the answer as 100815, instead of padding it to three digits as 015 to match the three zeros in the base 1000.
Losing the extra digit of the left part: with surpluses the left lane grows past the base to 1008, and it keeps all four digits in the final answer.
Adding a surplus to the wrong factor when checking crosswise, for example 1003 plus 3 instead of 1003 plus 5.
